reviews.author: Kim J.

reviews.text:
We celebrated our anniversary at Luna. Nice atmosphere, great service from hostess desk and especially by Sherice our waitress. Lemon spaghetti and focaccia was yummy. The branzino was forgettable. Nice evening UNTIL, the valet could not find our car keys!!!!!! 1.5 hours later after security was called and videos were watched and my husband and the valets scoured the parking lot and key rack, finally we had to disrupt my son's evening to bring us our spare keys ( a one hour drive round trip). As soon as we started the car with the spare the valet found our keys in another car. We originally had plans to continue our evening with friends but it was late so just went home.
We were told by front desk supervisor  who took our information that we would be called the next day and somehow compensated for their debacle but we never heard from anyone and it has been nearly a week. Feel like we should have at least gotten a phone call with an apology from upper management. 
Hope they get the valets organized and doesn't happen to someone else. Tip: Put an air tag on your keys if you visit Luna!
reviews.author: Bk L.

reviews.text: Luna by Giada surpassed our expectations from start to finish! All the staff were so friendly and greeted us with a smile but our waiter was the star of the night. Kenneth made us feel welcome, explained the menu, and made fabulous recommendations.  The Sicilian Foccocia, Seared Branzino, and Limoncello Soufflé were a few highlights.  Be prepared to pay Caesar's added 'venue' fee. Excellent choice for a family celebration.
reviews.author: James Z.

reviews.text: We had a special evening on the patio with Clyde and Parker as our servers.  They took special care of us as we were celebrating my mom's 91st birthday. The food was delish also! A memory for the books!
reviews.author: Julie A.

reviews.text: It was a fantastic evening at the restaurant. The atmosphere is very relaxing and everybody was very friendly. Our waitress Melanie made our evening there very nice for my sister and I. The ones she got out to taste complimented our choices very nicely... We would highly recommend the bacon-wrapped dates, they were fantastic!
reviews.author: Shonda W.

reviews.text: the food was incredible and love the atmosphere. haven't been here before and Hailey recommended this location to me, totally worth it!
reviews.author: Mark V.

reviews.text: My mom and I went for dinner last night for an early birthday celebration. Love to watch Giada and cook her recipes, so expectations were high - it didn't disappoint! The food was so good. The caprese salad and lemon spaghetti with shrimp was delicious. What made the night extra fun and delightful was our lovely server, Shereese. She made the night more of an experience and also treated my mom to a birthday dessert. We will be back!
reviews.author: Melissa H.

reviews.text:
Tonight we celebrated my husband's birthday. Brandy was our server. She was professional, extremely knowledgeable about the menu, kind, pleasant, and very attentive.  Brandy made the whole dining experience wonderful and will ask for her upon our next visit. 
As for the food, DELICIOUS. Brandy recommended the lemon spaghetti with shrimp. We added additional scallops. Both the shrimp and scallops were cooked to perfection! The spaghetti yummy. Did I mention the focaccia? Additionally, the lemon soufflé dessert was delightful. 
Lastly, on the way out the door, Brandy met us with two delicious cookies as we were leaving the restaurant backslash hotel.
You absolutely cannot go wrong by Dining at Luna.
reviews.author: Stephanie R.

reviews.text:
After reading the other reviews, we weren't sure what to expect from Luna. Thankfully, we had a good experience overall. 

We arrived a little prior to our reservation time and were seated promptly in the back section of the restaurant near the private dining room. The front of the restaurant is much louder than the back, so if you want a quieter experience, ask to be seated in the back or outside. Our server Rae was great, and she was friendly and efficient. My wife has some food allergies and restrictions, and our order was communicated well with the kitchen and came out accurately. Jose, our busser was very nice too and was always there to clear our plates or fill up water. One of the managers was making rounds and checking in with guests to make sure everything was going well. 

The food itself we had mixed opinions on. For appetizers, we shared the foccacia bread, caprese salad, and fritto misto. The bread was excellent, though a little heavy-handed with finishing salt on top. Caprese salad was very unique, full of flavor, and loved the balsamic pearls! Fritto misto was decent, but there was too much breading for the size of the squid tube that was cut. 

For entrees, we shared the lemon spaghetti and branzino. For being Giada's signature dish, the spaghetti was unfortunately underwhelming. The pasta itself was fresh, made, and cooked perfectly. However, there wasn't much lemon flavor and too much cream and cheese. It tasted more like an Alfredo sauce. Thankfully, the branzino made up for the spaghetti and was delicious. The crispy skin and toasted capers, along with hazelnut sauce, added the right amount of crunch to the dish and made it one of the better branzino dishes we've had in recent days. 

The highlight of our meal was dessert. We had the lemon blueberry souffle and chocolate orange ammoretti cake. Both were full of flavor, and the cake wasn't too heavy like a lot of similar cakes can be. 

So overall a good experience, but there is room for improvement in some of their dishes. We'll be back to try their pizza and other pastas. 

Also wanted to mention they do charge a 3.5% "admin fee." We're hoping this goes to employee healthcare, etc. A lot of restaurants are doing this now, and it's annoying. We'd rather they just include these fees with the food pricing so we don't see it billed separately.
reviews.author: Nathan B.

reviews.text:
Exceeded all expectations. 

Luna by Giada is a culinary gem that transports your tastebuds straight to Italy. Walking into Luna, we were greeted with a warm welcome from the hostess. The ambience is a perfect blend of modern elegance and an unforgettable dining experience, whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply indulging in a weekday treat. Started off with a refreshing La Strada. 
Appetizers were crab arancini and spicy sausage pizza, entrees: Giada's signature lemon spaghetti, Med. Branzino and a side of lemon smashed potatoes. Needless to say every dish is crafted with passion and precision by the talented chefs. So many amazing flavors that leave you craving more. Yes..yes somehow managed to make room for dessert cannot stress this enough the cheesecake is a must! 
The staff is friendly, knowledgeable, and always willing to go the extra mile to ensure your satisfaction. 

Luna By Giada is a must to experience.
reviews.author: Amanda T.

reviews.text:
I wanted to love this new Giada De Laurentiis restaurant, because, after all, who doesn't love Giada?
It was difficult obtaining a reservation for a Saturday night as all tables were booked for weeks, so we settled on a 9pm reservation. We arrived at 8pm, checked in with the hostess stand and told the young ladies we were early, but if available, we would like to be seated early. We went into the bar area to have a pre-dinner cocktail, socialize and wait to be called. The bartenders were friendly and prepared nice cocktails. We could see into the restaurant and noticed several open tables but, we waited...
At 9pm, my husband walked to the hostess stand to check on the status of our reservation and it was like they had forgotten about us. She said "Oh! We can take you now!" and off we went.  As we walked to the back of the restaurant, we saw at least 15-20 empty tables. I asked the hostess if there was a reason we were not able to be seated earlier? She said, "Your reservation was for 9pm!". A bit later a manager came over to apologize for the error, but seriously, how hard is it to seat your customers when you have many empty tables?
While we were at our table and our server was nice, but seemed stressed like maybe there was an understaffing problem, however mid way thru dinner, we noticed at least 5-6 young men all standing around chatting, not doing anything- and one of them was the manager.
At our table we ordered more cocktails and waited. A runner was walking thru the restaurant with this round black thing on a plate and I said to my husband, "Is that burnt bread? I hope they dont put that on our table!". Yep, sure enough, they delivered us burnt bread. We asked the waitress, "Is the bread supposed to be served burnt?" She said no. We had to ask, "Then why did they serve it to us burnt?" The server apologized and it was replaced with slightly less burnt bread.
We then ordered the Lobster Bucatini for two and added shrimp. When it arrived, the server, poured this lucious creamy red sauce all over the half lobster in the shell! When he walked away, we realized there was no serving utensils for plating the bucatini. We had 2 small salad or bread plates, 2 forks and 2 butter knives. No spoons, nothing to really place portions on plates and our only plates were tiny! We waited for awhile, no server came by and we had to eat our dinner on a giant platter in the middle of the table. I had to remove the lobster meat from the shell covered in red sauce with my fingers and a fork! It was the worst presentation ever--and  messy to eat!
To be fair, the lobster and the pasta was prepared well and the sauce was delicious! 
We did order the chocolate amaretti cake for dessert, but it was not that great and we didnt even eat it all. We each took a bite and just pushed it away.
reviews.author: K T.

reviews.text: Absolutely Stunning! Amazing! It's nothing like the experience you have at giada, also she's an amazing person, when you get to meet her. She's not a fake person nor a phony person that wants or needs your opinion.
reviews.author: Johnathan A.

reviews.text:
My husband and I had a wonderful dinner experience here tonight.
Our server Brandi was informative and very friendly. We started with the crab appetizer and the Focaccia  bread. Both were delicious. We ordered the signature Lemon pasta for our entree. It has two jumbo shrimp and we added two more. The dish was amazing and the shrimp were cooked perfectly. 
We ended with the brownie cheesecake. It did not disappoint. 
We look forward to visiting again soon and trying more items on the menu.
reviews.author: Lori T.

reviews.text: Excellent food and service!  Brandi was the best!!  Delicioso!!  We'll definitely be returning for this great experience!  Don't miss it!
reviews.author: Lorie M.

reviews.text:
Absolute garbage.

The food is mediocre, even the famous lemon pizza. Salmon was boring and the beans didn't jive with the dish. The petite filet was lukewarm warm and tasteless. Soooo many far better steaks (and restaurants) within shouting distance. 

The design of the restaurant is terrible. The back room is narrow and loud. Boring decor. Hard, bland surfaces galore. There is a door to the kitchen that swings open all the time for service and showers the room with bright hospital white light. Also, everyone in the back room is treated to not only a parade of people walking through he tables to use the restroom but because they are located on a straight hallway directly off the back room we can see everyone entering and leaving the bathrooms. The whole thing feels like an office building not a nice restaurant.

Shamefully, in the back room, there are only two POS kiosks for servers to enter orders so there's always a queue of servers waiting for the kiosk. What a waste of their time and slows things down for the customers. Service was subpar overall. 

The only bar is in the front, far away from the back room, and for some dumb reason they have the bartenders at the bar making drinks for the entire restaurant as well as the bar area. Drink service is incredibly slow.

The music is WAY too loud.

No view from the restaurant or bar.

They don't have prices on their online menu, a cardinal sin.

There is absolutely nothing special about this place as evidenced by the reviews here. We went with hardcore Gilda fans who were embarrassed and flabbergasted at everything about it.
reviews.author: Tom T.

reviews.text: We are big fans of Giada and wanted to try her new restaurant.  We went last Friday.  We sat on the patio out of the sun, and had a lovely evening.  We started with the appetizer of Fritto Miso, calamari and shrimp with little yellow peppers & squash blossoms, with a lemon aioli.  There were two very tiny squash blossoms so not really sure why they're there.  The shrimp was tasty but the calamari was tasteless, the breading was nice and light but it needs more seasoning.  For our main we split the Shellfish tower for two.  It had a great amount of fresh cold seafood, including huge shrimp, lobster, crab and oysters served with lemon mustard sauce, vinegarette and cocktail sauce.  It was plentiful, delicious and fresh.  We also had a side of the corn & sausage which is a very fancy version similar to Elote.  I had a glass of Prosecco and Boo had a glass of white, Maltide Greco.  For dessert we ordered the Tiramisu and Limoncello Soufflé to go,  We live fairly close so we went ahead with the soufflé to go even tho it's not recommended.  The Tiramisu is some of the best I've had.  The Soufflé was ok.  Neither really justified the hefty prices. $19 & $16 respectively    The Vegas pricing was a bit of sticker shock and it was a bit annoying to be charged for two bottles (2x$10) of Sparkling water since we only had one.  We like our waiter, Tucker and his assistant but he should have realized the overcharge.
reviews.author: Kathryn J.

reviews.text:
Food is excellent, everything is delicious from appetizers to main dishes. I will come back just for the food. 

However the wait & service is way too slow...
We had a reservation but we didn't get seated until 1hr later. Finally we got our seat, we got our menu but no one to take our order till another 30-40mins.
Our waitress is too busy chatting with other customers. My disappointed face was noticed by one waiter walking past me and he stopped and finally got our order in. 

Once the order was submitted, the food came really fast. Kitchen has plenty of workers, food is delicious. I just wish the wait time and service can match up with that.
reviews.author: Jessica L.

reviews.text: Went to Luna for the 1st time last night, very underwhelming. Prices are ridiculous, even for Scottsdale. Ambiance was nice, service left quite a bit to be desired. Our server was very slow with our drinks and entrees, but yet seemed to want to turn our table as quick as she could.( serving staff seemed very confused) Pasta dishes were good, but they should be for $38 each! Pizza was terrible, has a chemical taste to it, for $28 I expected a lot more for a personal pizza! Won't be going back anytime soon.
reviews.author: Rick Y.

reviews.text:
tried this new spot, luna by giada in the gorgeous caesar's republic hotel in scottsdale...
not surprisingly, the restaurant was beautifully done and the food was exquisite...
there were a few mishaps, starting with us being sat in the far back at a table next to the restrooms..  one of us went to speak to the manager and we were moved to the front of the restaurant which we appreciated.. the other thing that happened was our server spilled an espresso martini all over my sister's fendi purse. our server was extremely apologetic and we understand that accidents happen. our issue was that the purse is an expensive bag and it is now stained and smells like an espresso. while they did comp the drink and a dessert, the fact is, the purse is worth a couple thousand dollars and was hoping they would offer to get it cleaned. unfortunately we felt uncomfortable asking, so i guess it is something that we have to live with unfortunately.

aside from these things that happened, we did actually enjoy our meal...
we started with the caesar with crispy capers..  
then had the oysters with a simple and delicious prosecco mignonette..  
i had the braised pork & veal agnolotti en brodo..
sister had giada's lemon spaghetti with shrimp..
S had the scallops over a creamy risotto..
we tried the margherita pizza which we really liked.. 
and ended with tiramisu which was the only disappointment.. tiramisu is usually a light dessert but this was very thick and heavy.. it was more like a chocolate pudding..
but all in all, the food was amazing, the restaurant was beautiful & the service was good, which made for an yummy fun night with the besties...
it's too bad that our experience was tainted with an incident with an expensive bag that we need to find a way to clean now..

reviews.author: Rose C R.

reviews.text:
I was so excited to try Luna and booked my reservation 2 months in advance. The cocktails were fantastic and the spicy sausage pizza was the best thing we had.

For the price you pay (...honestly it's just because Giada's name is on the restaurant), the quality is not great. I would have had a much better meal for half the price at Pomo or North.

The agnolotti is incredibly small, the tripolini lacks flavor (and to add a tiny chicken breast it's an additional $16), and the pork chop ($66) is very plain with minimal sauce making it quite dry. 

For $30+ pastas, no entrees less than $50, and $21 cocktails, I was expecting to be wowed but that was unfortunately far from true.
reviews.author: Katie A.

reviews.text: We took the lemon tour at Luna and it was a pleasure. For cocktails, a Lemon Drop in an impressive glass was delicious. The moderno, essentially an old fashioned with a Super Tuscan float was a surprisingly good combination - recommended. The focaccia with lemon butter, olive oil with herbs, and just olive oil, was delish. Not a ton of lemon flavor in the lemon butter, but light with a crispy crust. The wait staff in general was perfectly attentive, not hovering, but appearing at just the right time for everything. Our primary server was a little too scripted, doing the annoying read of the menu with everything being a favorite. My wife was really looking forward to the lemon pizza. Honestly it's a bit much as an app for a party of two, super rich and sweet for our taste in appetizers. Caesar was great, and the lemon spaghetti was remarkable with a silky but not too rich sauce. The lemon soufflé was a home run, one of the best we've ever had, an airy lemon pillow of yumminess, a must. The vibe was what you would expect for Giada and Caesars - felt like Vegas. To top it off we heard so many "so good" comments from other tables. We will be back.
reviews.author: Ed L.

reviews.text: We had the focaccia and crab arancini. Both were phenomenal and would recommend! Was really hoping the pastas were gonna be just as dynamite but unfortunately the nodi alla vodka flavor was like a grown up Mac and cheese and the mezzi rigatoni was just okay. Rigatoni was definitely better of the two and the noodles were nice and al dente. Tiramisu was very good. Our hostess was great.
reviews.author: Kayla T.

reviews.text:
Classy looking entry to Caesars and a cool bar, although a tad sterile. Good drink menu if that's your thing, but $21 cocktails won't pull me back in.

Restaurant is a huge space; tables are spaced nicely apart so you don't feel like people are sitting on top of each other. 

Service was solid - waiter was professional and knowledgeable about the menu and recommendations. 

Wine list was far from extensive and there's no bargains to be found - have a bottle at home before you come.

We started with a pizza as an appetizer - spicy sausage that had no spice in either the sausage or peppers. Crust was super light and good.

Three of us had pasta dishes (all $30-$40) and I went with our waiter's recommendation of the pork chop saltimbocca. Nice concept, but really just a pounded chop like schnitzel. He touted the melted cheese dripping everywhere over the breaded crust as you cut into it, but the shaved parm wasn't melted at all. This $60 dish was bland and overcooked, and terribly disappointing.

The pasta were ok - nothing outstanding or special at all, and certainly not even close to worth the price.

End of the night, we had 4 drinks at the bar (+$100), pizza, 3 entrees, bottle of Pinot and a glass of Santa Margarita. This was a $500 night and hardly any part was worth it.

I have a few of Giada's cookbooks - that's as close as I'd advise anyone get to this menu.

(2 stars for a super friendly waiter)
reviews.author: Scot A.

reviews.text: I hardly ever post bad reviews but my experience here last night was horrible. My friends and I had reservations at 7:45 PM and didn't get seated until 8 PM. The table wasn't ready and we asked to move inside when they were clearly tables available we had to sit outside, which was fine. The hostess was clueless and had no idea what was going on. We didn't get menus or Utensils until 30 minutes after sitting down. Our waiter was OK but the food took forever and we didn't end up getting out of the restaurant until 10 PM. I don't recommend this place even though the food was good.
reviews.author: Natasha H.

reviews.text:
It is so disappointing to write this review. I've been waiting to go to Luna for my parents to come into town from Michigan. First, we waited 20 minutes for our server to come to our table and when I asked for any recommendations he said "can I get you a drink first" rudely and I just said any drink suggestions. He noted he had another table he was needing to go to and left. Another 10 minutes go by and we have a new waitress, Suzanne. Very lovely. We ordered focaccia and oysters, which were good. Ordered 4 entrees to come out in two waves, per servers advice. The 2nd round of entrees came out and we didn't have plates or flatware. It took 10 minutes for another server to notice and come bring us plates. He said "I didn't want your food getting any more cold". At this point I was frustrated, since it was a last night together dinner with my parents and when they brought the bill, it had an additional pizza and was $400. I asked for a manager and expressed how upsetting this experience was since my mother had been so excited. They took off our $60 bottle of wine from our bill and said they were "sending us with to go desserts". 5 minutes later we were given our new $320 bill and 4 prepackaged cookies, which were lack luster. I truly hate having to give reviews like this but with the amount of quality restaurants from maple & ash, pyro, steak 44, bourbon and bones, and more... I would choose elsewhere for a better experience. I'm happy to pay for quality but unfortunately, this restaurant and staff left me missing the Scottsdale staples everyone knows and loves.

We were also told we'd get a phone number for a direct line and receive 50% off our next visit... that never came. I'd rather receive a complete refund and move on from this experience.
reviews.author: Erika E.

reviews.text:
Well my wife twisted my arm to try this new restaurant and I really wish that it was worth the visit. First let's discuss the food. We ordered Focaccia bread and calamari/shrimp. The bread was ok but very salty got that. When we tried the shrimp it was really bad, smelly and rotten so we immediately returned the dish less one bite. The bar tender was  very understanding so we ordered a pasta dish instead. Well that wasn't any better the sauce was soooo  salty and frankly that dish didn't taste good either. We bit our tongue  as not to sound like customers that nothing makes them happy. We had three cocktails that were ok as well.
The  only bright spot was the bar tenders attitude and I will give them 5 stars just for that otherwise it will be a one star rating review and not two stars.
It was a bad and pricy experience as compared to other fine dining establishments in Scottsdale..
My advice is for the restaurant management and chef to taste and smell the food before they serve itt to customers No wonder Luna only ihas a 3.5 star average rating that I just saw before writing this review.
reviews.author: Mike S.

reviews.text: Great atmosphere! Fantastic food and service, awesome focaccia bread and lemon pasta!
reviews.author: Lauren H.

reviews.text: Went to Luna by Giada's last night for our anniversary dinner. The food was outstanding. My husband had the Risotto with Scallops and I had the Nodi Marini Alla Vodka. We had the focaccia bread for an appetizer.  They served it with a lemon marscapone cheese butter, as well as olive oil with balsamic vinegar and an olive oil with pesto for dipping. Outstanding! Elegant yet simple. Highly recommend! Service was outstanding! Really go above and beyond!
reviews.author: Deb P.

reviews.text: Our food connoisseur Shereese curated a beautiful experience for us. She asked insightful questions to assess our palette and guide the experience. The food and drinks were wonderful and delivered with expert timing. The service was the best I've experienced & the focaccia and lemon pasta lived up to the hype.
reviews.author: Mandi R.

reviews.text: The food was delilcious, the service superb and the ambiance perfect at Luna by Giada at Caesar's Republic last night! We enjoyed a six-person family dinner and among us we had imaginiative drinks and a variety of beatuiful looking and tasting dishes. The SIgnature lemon pasta was superb as was the salmon with beans, the pizzas were just right -- looks, size and taste--including a new one for us-lemon pizza and the caprese was the best any of us had eaten. Somehow we managed to eat all the tiramisu, too--wow!
reviews.author: Laraine R.

reviews.text: Service was great, food not so much, extremely over priced. We had Caprese salad( good) arancini( good). pasta was ok, steak had to send back, pork chop was super thin and dry and fish was very small portion and dry for $50. Ambiance of bar was nice- restaurant felt partially like you were still in the lobby. Dessert was also so bland-was cheesecake brownie- no sweetness or tart of cheesecake. Nothing was wow by any means and extremely over priced- bummer considering it's Giadas place. Would rather go to an authentic italian restaurant for half the price twice the deliciousness. Also they add a $20credit card processing fee to your bill- never seen that before!
reviews.author: Tktash K.

reviews.text: The service was really good. Annette and Andy were really attentive. The decor of the lobby and the ambiance of the restaurant were spectacular. Unfortunately most of the food misses its mark especially at its price points. The Agnolotti was a solid 7/10 - had good flavor, balance and texture. Focaccia was moist but super salty. And the Crab Arancini was really bland and not even the dipping sauce could help flavor it. It was nice to see a soufflé on the menu but at best it was still only decent. As a resort type restaurant it's not terrible. However, there are certainly better restaurants to choose from in the valley.
reviews.author: Brandon Y.

reviews.text: Horrible! Horrible! Horrible! Adding insult to injury... we were CHARGED a "3.5% Venue Admin Fee" and when I asked the 4 hostesses, they knew nothing. I requested to speak with the manager, and was told he would be right out. TEN MINUTES LATER.... I finally got to speak with the manager, and was told this was a CREDIT CARD PROCESSING FEE!!!! So deceptive! Such a Bullshit charge for an overpriced menu for mediocre food! We will NEVER go back!
reviews.author: Jack M.

reviews.text: Love Giada but wouldn't go back again. Luna is overpriced with slow food service (at least 45 minutes) and average trained wait staff. $24 margaritas... lol...no wow factor for that price. Thank goodness the place had some ambiance.
reviews.author: Tim T.

reviews.text:
What can they improve. It's evident that Giada has not tasted the food Luckily i have been brought up around some of the best NY italian restaurants and sadly i must critique my experience. first the good news the manager was not only nice but attentive ., as was waitress .
let's start with the perfectly tasteless , over breaded and greasy frito misto. Costcos calamari is like a gourmet dinner in Positano . 
now let's move on to her supposed signature dish , I guess the lemon pasta. yes it had 2  I say 2 medium 
at best shrimp for .$40 . it was 1pasta and 1.50 of Shrimp, embarrassing and tasted like wallpaper paste . the wine was marked up 4  times the cost. . 
I think Giada might want to beat Bobby Flay. where i have loved him from Mesa Grill to Bar Americano,
i hope she works hard on this  to improve because i would like to come back .
ps  if you don't have table cloths , have nice placements on the table. Wendy's tables are nicer .
reviews.author: Scott B.

reviews.text:
I made a reservation online a few weeks in advance for Saturday evening dinner as a late bday surprise for my sister. Booking was easy and quick. 

The day finally came and we arrived at the establishment right on time for our reservation. We luckily found a parking spot right away as we saw many cars circling the lot for a spot. Valet was also available. We walked in and we were both quickly greeted by the host. She was very soft spoken and told us it would be a few minutes for our table so we stood to the side.

Once ready, she came over to get us and walked us to our table. It was very loud inside so it was hard to hear her. She showed us the merch wall and told us those items were available for purchase. She then walked us over to one of the tables inside but then decided to take us outside onto the patio.

We sat down, she gave us our menus, and she let us know our server would be right out. While looking over the menu, another person came by and filled up our glasses with water. He was on his A game as he kept us refilled the whole night. Our server came over a few minutes later and gave us the 411. She gave us a few minutes and we proceeded to order. We ordered:

CAPRESE SALAD - Heirloom Tomatoes, Stracciatella Cheese, Basil & Balsamic Pearls / $23
LEMON PIZZA - Mozzarella, Garlic Crème Sauce & Caciocavallo Cheese  $28
ROASTED BROCCOLINI - Parmigiano Reggiano, Roasted Garlic Oil, Lemon Zest / $17

LIMOCELLO SOUFFLE: Blueberry anglaise & candied lemon biscotti / $14
LA ESTRADA COCKTAIL: Stoli cucumber vodka, belle de brillet, re'al kiwi puree, lemon juice, club soda / $21

The salad came out right away and we were quickly disappointed as we took our first bites. All the tomatoes had a different consistency. Some were very mushy, some were ripe, some tasted funky, and some of them tasted old. The cheese they were sitting on was more of like a yogurt and the whole combination was a big no for us - we did not finish it....

Next was the pizza and broccolini. The pizza was a pass for me but a hit for my sister. She really liked that it was both sweet and salty. I thought the crust was pretty good as it was baked perfectly. The broccolini was a side that we both agreed on that was very delicious!!! They were flavorful, crunchy, and super tasty! I would order that over and over again!!

I had La Estrada drink and it too was a pass... It tasted very watered down and had no flavor. Definitely not worth the $21 price point. The Limocello Soufflé was pretty good as it was served to us warm topped with a pink sauce and they added a cute Happy Birthday chocolate on top. 

Service was ok. Not sure if our server would forget we were seated outside or whatever but we did a lot of sitting around waiting for her to come by.  The patio area was quiet as it was just us two and another party of two eating outside.

Views are great, the food was meh. Not sure I'd be back. 

Grand total: $145 with tip
reviews.author: Christa M.

reviews.text:
I really enjoyed my dinner and cucumber drink. The scallops were well prepared and the souffle was the best that I have ever had. I thoroughly appreciated our server, Melanie, who was competent, friendly, and helpful when ordering.
I wish there was live music in the bar or lobby for more ambiance. I will return to try other dishes.
reviews.author: Katherine K.

reviews.text:
My mom and I dined at Luna by Giada. We made our reservation about a month ago and have been so excited to try. Immediately upon arrival we were greeted with friendly faces and superior service. We checked out the roof top bar as well as the bar in Luna. The drinks are pricey but as expected in old town Scottsdale. The food selection was so unique and absolutely delicious. We tried the focaccia, bacon dates, vodka pasta, as well as the filet. For prices, just expect the same compared to every other restaurant in old town Scottsdale. Except here the food and service is worth the money! Our server Shereese went absolutely above and beyond. As well as Tony. He was so kind. They made the entire experience that much better with their friendly service and extensive knowledge. We will definitely be back again soon!! 
I would also like to add that this gave me a very European style of dinner.. the way each individual dish is brought out separately and meant to be shared, it was a wonderful experience.
reviews.author: Bella F.

reviews.text: Went tonight and my husband and I were greeted by Jay our waiter. We explained to him that we are vegetarian, and he made recommendations for us. We started with the Caesar salad, followed by the Mezzi Rigatoni, and then tried the lemon pizza, and for dessert we had the MASCARPONE BROWNIE CHEESECAKE. We shared all the dishes which were absolutely delicious. The service was incredible, Jay was very attentive, checking that everything was just perfect, and the staff always made sure our water was filled and table was clean. We highly recommend Luna and will be back!!
reviews.author: Caryn F.

reviews.text:
Hi Giada! I've been following you for years on Food Network & have been a big fan of all your cookbooks! 

My significant other took me tonight for my 47th birthday to your new restaurant Luna in Old Town Scottsdale, AZ. 

Unfortunately, it was the worst restaurant experience that I've ever had. For my birthday, they threw 2 plastic wrapped cookies at me as if it was at McDonald's "happy meal". It was very disheartening & tacky! Especially, after ordering apps, entrees & a bottle of wine...along with/ cocktails earlier in the evening. Even when the server approached the manager... The manager said this is how we do it from now on. 

I will still continue to purchase your cookbooks, but doubt that I will ever return to one of your establishments ever again. 

Very disappointed
reviews.author: April P.

reviews.text: I always love trying restaurants whose chef's recipes  I have made over the years. I liked the ambiance, the menu was good but the service was average at best. Our sides arrived after we completed our entrees. In their defense they did offer to remove from our bill. We were celebrating a 55th bday and there were 7 in attendance and we were brought 2 cookies for the table  There are so many amazing restaurants in Scottsdale and sadly this one fell very short a month in :(. I would absolutely bypass and go to Scott Conant's Mora Italian.
reviews.author: Kimberly H.

reviews.text: Love Giada but very disappointed with the service food was mediocre at best and took forever. Our server disappeared between appetizers and entree. After 25 min he came by and said he didn't know why the chef didn't prepare our food and he would check. After another 15 min the food came out he never refilled our water wanted hot pepper flakes by couldn't find him. 14.00 for bread!! Then I ordered an expresso and it came out cold... very disappointing...
reviews.author: Art P.

reviews.text: Where to begin! The overall experience was amazing from the moment we walked in to the moment we left! Our server was Tucker and he was truly spectacular! He was so patient and informative about every single item on the menu and I think he spent a solid 20 minutes answering all of questions just about the wine! Every item we ordered was amazing - the focaccia, caprese salad, nodi alla vodka, tripolini pasta, and my favorite, as recommended by Tucker, the scallop risotto! The ambiance was great and lively and we cannot wait to come back again! 1000/10! Make sure to finish the meal with the tiramisu!
reviews.author: Alexis W.

reviews.text: LAME! Got there 5 minutes before reservation and had to wait an additional 15 before being sat. Service was so slow. Had three glasses of water before my drink came. We were comped our first round of drinks at least. Food is basic. Crab arancini were fried cheese balls??? Definitely trying to be fancier than the food actually is. Your basic mom and pop outshines this place by a mile.
reviews.author: Bianca M.

reviews.text: The environment is beautiful. The service and food need some work for the price. Give them some time to fine tune and I'm sure they will rise to the occasion.
reviews.author: Christina S.

reviews.text: Went to Luna tonight, I have to say really enjoyed it! Appetizers very good, honestly awesome capris salad, crab arancini,  birthday girl had the lemon pasta, awesome! $67 steak ok, little undercooked but not complaining! Little over salted, beautiful ambiance! Good job Giada! Preston and Jose were impressive! Getting there girl! You will do well! Happy bday Jade tomorrow!
reviews.author: Mia C.

reviews.text: Somewhat disappointing other than good pizza.  The staff was lovely but not everybody knew the menu...when we were told a dish was red sauced based, it wasn't, so they offered a side of sauce but then charged for it.  Decent portion size but no bread or side salad for the price.  Very average food for an expensive meal.
reviews.author: Amy W.

reviews.text: I really wanted this to be a five star as I am a big fan of Giada. But this was very disappointing. My girlfriends and I went out for a special dinner and celebration. I made reservations weeks in advance and when we got there, we had to wait for our table for 15-20 minutes. Then when we got sat down, we waited another 20-30 minutes for a server. There was no water and some of us were missing napkins. We finally got water 30 minutes later and the server was sweating profusely when he got to us. The menus were cheap paper. When we finally ordered food came out fast but the bread was burnt, dates were cold, and some of our pasta dishes were cold. They forgot to offer knives to us to we had to wait for those. It was very disappointing. I've been to her restaurant in Las Vegas and it was a stellar, five-star experience.  Not sure what's going on here but for $40 a plate of food, it was not worth it.
reviews.author: Ashley S.

reviews.text:
** I would give our server 5 stars!! But this is mainly a food review **

 I have been to Giada's restaurant in Vegas multiple times so I was excited to make reservations to Luna almost a month in advance when I booked my trip to Pheonix. We were early so we went upstairs to Seven which is another lounge/bar area. When our table was finally ready we were excited to get started. We ordered a few cocktails and some appetizers. The cocktails took longer than necessary to arrive with one of them not being correct. The focaccia bread was amazing, and so are the rest of the appetizers that we got. We ordered the signature lemon pasta, the risotto, and the lemon pizza. The signature lemon pasta was underwhelming. The sauce was runny, which we were told that is the way it was supposed to be. The shrimp that were company the pasta were slightly overcooked in a bit fishy smelling. But the main issue with the pasta was that it was barely warm. Moving onto the lemon pizza - how do white sauce that was very running on it which was kind of interesting to see on a pizza. The cress itself was tasty but the lemon that they had on top left a bitter taste. Definitely not like the lemons in Italy but I digress. The risotto had to get flavors but also, not warm. He ordered one dessert which was the soufflé. That had a good flavor. We did chat with the manager and told him our concerns with some of the food which he took well. Their overall ambience is great and it's a beautiful restaurant. But the food needs some work. Our server was amazing and we had a good time with him.
reviews.author: Jenn P.

reviews.text: My husband and I were very excited to try this restaurant since we love Giada's restaurant in Las Vegas. We were disappointed to say the least. When we arrived, no one was at the front desk. We stood there for a while. As we waited, I looked around and was completely underwhelmed by the environment. We took seats at the bar after finally speaking to the hostess. We were early so already planned on having a drink before dinner. None of the three female bartenders acknowledged our existence for quite some time. It wasn't busy. When one bartender finally came over, there was no smile, no welcome, just a menu. We had two specialty cocktails that tasted like cough syrup and enjoyed each other's company until the hostess came to seat us.  I would also like to mention that not only were the bartenders unfriendly, but our first drinks sat 90% empty for a long time and we were never offered another round. I paid 60 dollars for two cocktails and horrible service! We were sat right next to the restrooms even though several other tables were available. There is no wall or divider, so you just sit there watching people come in and out of the restroom. Gross. We asked to move and that process took too long. We were finally seated at a four top facing the kitchen. Much better table, but I sat there and watched a kitchen employee eat the entire time we were there. I'm pretty sure that behavior should be discouraged. Our server was nice but clearly untrained and inexperienced. He never cleared away the two extra place settings and he never brought the bottle of Prosecco we ordered, We had to flag down a manager. The food was blah, the dessert was okay, and the service throughout was spotty and confusing. This was not a positive experience right from the beginning. I guess we will wait until our next trip to Vegas to eat at Giada's.
reviews.author: Jennifer S.

reviews.text:
Was looking forward to the experience for quite a while as we had made the reservation 3 weeks in advance. We were a party of 2 and  our reservation was during a later part of the evening. The business seemed to be steady but not overcrowded or extremely busy by any means. We ordered 2 drinks and the bread to start. Our sever did not remember who had which drink (which typically is not a big deal) but I think speaks to the lack of attentiveness to detail and timeliness when added to our other concerns. Our water was never refilled, and it took 45 minutes for the bread to finally arrive at our table after ordering. After waiting for 1.5 hours for our food (2 entrees) we decided that we could wait no longer and let the hostess know that we would be leaving.

It would be one thing if the staff were frequently checking in and updating us as to why it was taking so long for anything to show up at our table, but this did not happen. We only had the bread and 2 drinks. They were mediocre at best. Would not recommend risking wasting an important day celebrating here.
reviews.author: Cody B.

reviews.text: Everything was as good if not better than Giada Las Vegas! Food, atmosphere and service. Definitely returning.
reviews.author: Gregory W.

reviews.text:
We went to Luna by Giada at the new Caesars republic hotel. This modern Italian restaurant is huge and perfect for large group reservation or a dinner date. The menu has a nice selection of many Italian dishes and we opted for a pizza/pasta combo which is perfect for us.

The service here was amazing despite the fact that this is a newer restaurant and you can tell that they really want you to have a great experience. This place is a bit pricey for an Italian concept, so I would recommend only coming here if you want to do a special occasion.

Overall, This is the best new Italian restaurant concept within the Old Town area, and will definitely be going back for a special occasion!
reviews.author: Ashkan A.

reviews.text:
This would be a convenient option for before or after a movie at Harkins Camelview, so we were looking forward to trying it out. First, the service was great overall, and our server was wonderful. The food was a little hit or miss. The focaccia bread was delicious, and we both enjoyed the caesar salad as well. The rigatoni with vegetarian bolognese was my favorite dish that we tried. The lemon spaghetti with shrimp was very bland and cold, and the tiramisu was just ok (more like a very rich chocolate pudding). The cocktails were a nice surprise and very nice and refreshing (we had the La Strada and Bella Luna). 

One of the things that was really disappointing was the wine list. It is a very boring selection of wines you can get for $10-20 at any grocery store (Cakebread, Duckhorn, etc.). Not terrible, but the markup was absolutely ridiculous ($110 for Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc as an example). Nothing that exciting even for the Italian wine selections either. For an Italian restaurant in this price range, I would definitely expect a little more. 

The ambiance/decor was ok. It looks nice but feels a little sterile, and I did not care for the strong fragrance in the lobby that carries into the restaurant a bit. The location is very odd with views of parking lots and the parking garage at the mall. The price for the dinner was very high for the quality of food, and there was a 3.5% venue access charge added as well which didn't help with our final impressions. Overall, we both agreed that we probably do not need to come back any time soon.
reviews.author: Jen A.

reviews.text:
I was excited to try this newly opened restaurant.  First I was disappointed they add a 3.5% venue charge based on your total bill. Shameful as other high end restaurants in the area don't even do that.  They should have researched the AZ market to know this shouldn't do this.  Get this taken off your bill, don't pay it since they don't disclose they add it!!! 
They serve vegan and gluten-free options, but the server never asked if anyone at our table had food allergies. Which is odd, because we did have allergy restriction to shellfish.  
Overall the food was good not great for the high prices and portion size.
reviews.author: S L.

reviews.text: Overall amazing experience. Our waiter was fantastic. His family is from Italy and we had the most amazing time with him. He had the best recommendations. The ambience is great for any occasion. The hotel itself has very modern pleasing decor. The restaurant is also decorated impeccably. We loved the atmosphere. The food was also fantastic. We got the 32 oz porter house for our main and weren't disappointed. I additionally recommend the caprese salad and the tiramisu.
reviews.author: Tisa K.

reviews.text: The space is beautiful but your view is of the street.  Wine list is spendy and not very diverse.  When you order your $25 dollar martini be prepared to pay extra for olives.  Food is the biggest disappointment. Not a single dish was out standing. At $145 a head for pasta i would have liked to be wowed.  I wouldn't bother
reviews.author: Jill C.

reviews.text: The food was way over my expectations, it was delicious! the service was top notch and the customer attention was top notch. Definitely recommend coming here for any event!
reviews.author: Parker M.

reviews.text:
Had dinner last night after watching Giadas show for so many years. I had an opportunity to be in italy last summer for the first time. I watched her travel show to Italy before coming to dinner and I wanted to see for myself. Let me tell you, it was fantastic. Started with the arancini and then of course had the signature lemon pasta. just the right amount of lemon and cheese and the homemade pasta was incredible with the perfect al dente. My friends had the lobster pasta and was wowed by the presentation. After a while, we had forgotten to take more pictures as my friends were recounting our trip to Italy. Cocktails were super refreshing as well.  
This is a must stop for any Italian aficionado. Let the restaurant team take you on an Italian food escape and you will not be disappointed.
reviews.author: Wil L.

reviews.text:
I would have liked to give this place a better rating but I just can't. It's another trendy, overpriced and overhyped restaurant in Scottsdale.
The good:  staff are very nice and try really hard but need more polish and better organization. The restaurant has a nice vibe overall but can be noisy. 
The not-so-good:  server was overly enthusiastic and big on the upsell. I understand that I guess but everything is overpriced. Fine dining prices for small portions and food that is average at best. No bread served with meals unless you order and pay $$ for it. Seems strange for an Italian restaurant! 
Summary:  Good, but far from great. This place really feels like a chain restaurant. There are much better places for Italian food out there and honestly, Olive Garden is one of them - lol!  We won't be going back.
reviews.author: Dorothy B.

reviews.text:
Was really excited to try this as I love Giada's cooking style and ate at her restaurant in Vegas at the Cromwell.  I thought it might be a fun spot for a girls night dinner and it was delicious.  
We started with the 'vaguely Virgil' cocktails.... So refreshing and a nice alternative to an aperol spritz as this has Prosecco, elderflower, lemon juice and a few other ingredients. 
We shared the crab arancini-  fantastic and bc I don't care for crab I was really happy that they were mild. They were cheesy and cooked to perfection with a tasty tomato dipping sauce. 
We also shared some focaccia and her signature lemon spaghetti.   They were both wonderful.  There are only 2 shrimp total on this dish ( there should be 4 imo) and the crispy capers are a nice touch.   The sauce is quite rich with marscarpone and Parmesan cheeses so happy that we shared.  
We also ordered some of her cookies to go.... Love those lemon ricotta ones. 
While the food was great, the prices are a bit steep for the portions.  And same goes for the cocktails.  But it's hard to get a drink at any restaurant in Scottsdale under $20 it seems...
Lastly, the hostess staff was friendly and engaging, which is not always the case and was definitely noticeable.
reviews.author: Robin P.

reviews.text: Let me start by saying the place is beautiful and the service was very good.  I know the place just opened 10 days ago so you have to give it time... I hope. The Frito Misto was tender but, lacked flavor and the coating on the delicate fish/vegetable was too much and you could taste the oil that it was fried in. The Pork Saltimbocca the breading again was thick and you could taste the fried oil.  We had a couple of other items which were very good such as the Chicken Panzanella and the Lemon Spaghetti.  The kicker is the CC charge on your bill of 3.5% (credit card charge) of your total bill that is crazy.  Most people will paying  using a credit card.  We go out all the time to all types of restaurants here in Arizona and this is the first restaurant we encountered this....just wrong.
reviews.author: Maria M.

reviews.text:
It pains me to not give 5 stars but our group of 5 were VERY underwhelmed. The signature cocktails were WAY too sweet...specifically the espresso martini. We ordered the oysters and burrata for appetizers. 10/10 on the oysters. Burrata was way over salted. We shared a few pastas. Lobster bucatini was good but the lobster was quite chewy and overcooked. I enjoyed a few bites of the lemon pasta and scallop risotto but nothing was out of this world. 
The ambience in the back of the restaurant is very blah. No charm to that space. When we finished dinner, walking through the entrance of the restaurant seemed like a much more exciting vibe. If I visited again, I would specify to sit there instead of the back room. As far as the wait staff goes, my input would be to focus more on customer experience. There was nothing that made this experience special. There was zero class or charm from the employees which I think most prefer when dining at an expensive restaurant.
reviews.author: Erin F.

reviews.text: Food, drinks, and ambience was 10/10. The Chef, CJ and the rest of the staff went above and beyond to make the night feel special for my friends and I. Good recommendations for this place. Also, go for the lemon pizza. You won't try it anywhere else in AZ!
reviews.author: Denise M.

reviews.text: So fortunate to enjoy date night at the newly opened restaurant in Scottsdale.  The beautiful hotel is the perfect spot for Giada's restaurant!  The food was outstanding and featured Giada's "pillars" which are lemon, parmigiana Reggiano, and Lucini olive oil!  The flavors in everything were clearly orchestrated!  The cocktails so refreshing!  The silver lining was our Server Seth, who made it an experience.  He guided us through the photos on the walls of the rooms.  Check out the Jade room.  The constellations represent the day she was born.  Did I say that from check in to every server . . Kind and Karing
reviews.author: Jacqueline B.

reviews.text: The food was amazing, from the starters captures salad to the dates and a must Focaccia bread. Loved the BrazIno and the pasta that's starts with a T . You must also try the cheesecake brownie and chocolate chip cookies are to die for. Our server Prescott we thought he's a chief cause he was so knowledgeable of the menu. We messed with him and he made our experience a fun one.
reviews.author: Linda Z.

reviews.text: Gave it a shot even with the negative reviews, sadly it was worse. The food is horrible, maybe the worst agnolotti I have ever had, it's basically a weird brown soup with a few pieces in it. We tried to order two basic cocktails, both times the waiter came back saying they didn't know how to make it or didn't have ingredients. The white pizza was bad, slightly cold. Too much lemon in every dish. Focaccia is good - that's it. The rest of the pastas were ok at best, horrendous for the price point. Embarrassing look for this new hotel concept. Highly do not recommend going here. Random 3% charge they put also - waste of time and money to dine here.
reviews.author: Drai V.

reviews.text: Food was very average and overpriced. Service was really great and cocktails okay but nothing to be impressed about. Happy to have new restaurants here but unfortunately the quality of food is not worth the price. The focaccia was the best item we had. Didn't care for any of the pastas or pizzas. Desserts were good.
reviews.author: Kayla O.

reviews.text: It has been 10 days or so since I have been trying to change my reservation from outdoors, to indoors.  I have left so many messages, and I have left a written request on Open Table.  NO one at the restaurant has taken the time to get back to me.  You cannot modify the reservations on Open Table they ask you to call the restaurant.
reviews.author: Linda G.

reviews.text:
Walking in, the restaurant was beautiful. Perfect lighting, noise level, and energy. We had a reservation at the bar, and the incredible hostess accommodated our reservation even though the bar was packed!! She was wonderful! Then we met Marcus, our bartender, and we can't say enough great things about him! He told me about their specialty margarita that wasn't on the menu yet! He told us about the thyme infused simple syrup they use in the margarita - it makes it so delicious!!
Then we got the Sicilian Focaccia and the Crab Arancini starters... all on Marcus's suggestion, and as he said - they were the bomb!! So delicious we were so excited about them. For our entree we got the Signature Lemon Spaghetti and it was fabulous!!! Can't recommend this place, and Marcus, enough!
reviews.author: Savanna J.

reviews.text:
Enjoyed dinner at Luna by Giada, it was good, Caesars Republic is really cool. I ordered bacon wrapped dates, scallop risotto and la strada for my cocktail, I would recommend them all. We originally booked a reservation on the patio but were sat in the Jade room, the hostess immediately resat us on the patio, it was nice outside, glad there were heat lamps. A large party sat after us, ordered after us, but received all their food before our entrées came out, which we found odd, but other than that, good experience, staff were very nice. 
I wish Giada would add more Gluten Free options to her menu, like pizza and pasta, I was disappointed, I would've loved to try the lemon spaghetti if there was a gf modification, and there should be another dessert option besides gelato and sorbet.
reviews.author: Gretchen B.

reviews.text: The best lemon soufflé I can imagine. Incredible food. Better service. A restaurant you wouldn't wanna miss.
reviews.author: Delaney C.

reviews.text: Wow!!  Luna is an excellent dining experience!  The scallop risotto entree was exceptional, and we couldn't get enough of the arancini appetizer.  But what really made the dining experience unforgettable was our cute and charming waiter, Melanie.  Melanie had great advice on what to order and gave her service with that glowing smile!  We love Giada and she's got a winner in her new restaurant, Luna.
reviews.author: Mary K.

reviews.text: The service was amazing and very prompt, the GM and staff were very attentive. The food was awesome, the filet was very good. The risotto was slightly undercooked for my wife but overall a great experience.
reviews.author: Keanan B.

reviews.text:
my wife and I had hoped for more last Friday night but... food portions are average and overpriced, the rear dining area is dark and 
decorated in a sparse way how about some pictures of Giada???
you will want to sit in the room with kitchen view 
menu is small selection wait staff is inexperienced 
we might? go back again sometime maybe too many other choices in PV Scottsdale area
reviews.author: Richard N.

reviews.text: Saturday night opening week. Beautiful restaurant, but we were in the Jade room facing a private glass room with a fake fire in a tv. We wish the private room had a curtain so we weren't staring at them and the tacky fake fire. Our service was great. We were told the food was served family style. It's not, the food portions are very small. We ordered the Agnolotti. For $41 you receive basically 4 ravioli cut in half. It was good and the broth flavorful. We had the corn and sausage side that was more filling than the agnolotti. The Amaretti cake for dessert. Again delicious but it's about 4 bites. Very limited wine by the glass menu starting at $17 for 6oz. The prices are crazy high, plus a 3.5% admin fee on every check & the portions are very small. We left still a little hungry.
reviews.author: Carey S.

reviews.text:
We were very excited to try Luna. Our entire experience from getting drinks at Seven to dining at Luna was very poor quality in service and taste. 
Luna's atmosphere felt similar to a cafeteria with the bright lights and boring decor. The staff seemed annoyed to be working or apathetic. Food was overpriced for the quality. Very disappointed. 
This was nothing like Giada's Vegas restaurants.
reviews.author: Kristin W.

reviews.text: Luna was amazing!  We dined three days after they opened and thought it was wonderful.  Had great service from Savannah - great energy, knew everything about the menu, gave great suggestion and SMIILED all the time.  Parker kept an eye on our table and kept us neat and hydrated.  Truly a team effort. Anyone that we had contact with - food delivery, water service, etc. was GREAT. EVERYONE was very happy, helpful and knowledgeable.  The food was great. Lemon SpaghettI was very tasty.  Didn't feel rushed as we had appetizers and salads.  Timing of entrees was perfect. Everything we tried was good and nice portions.  So glad we went and will be back.
reviews.author: S K.

reviews.text: Highly recommend Luna by Giada! The food and the entire experience is Amazing! By far, the most wonderful and attentive staff who goes above and beyond. Ray the GM does an amazing job and takes good care of all the guests to make everyone feel extra special and provides that extra special touch and truly goes above and beyond. Our server was Brandi and she was amazing, very attentive, knowledgeable on the entire menu, offered great suggestions, very personable and made our table feel extra special. All the servers worked together as a "Team" and displayed such a genuine desire to ensure your experience was amazing! Server Landiss stopped by our table, saw we were enjoying our wine and recommended others to try for our next visit. Big shout out to Hayden who not only cleared our table after each entrée he was beyond personable made suggestions and simply made sure we were taken care of. This consistent and outstanding service is what makes our stay extra special and beyond memorable!!! Keep up the class act!!! This is a perfect example for other restaurants to follow!!! Great Job to All!!! So Glad we finally have an authentic Italian restaurant that is now our Go To venue! Very Happy Customer, Kim M.
reviews.author: Kim M.

reviews.text:
Sat for drinks in the bar area.

Service was outstanding, particularly Parker and Savannah, both super-enthusiastic and attentive.

Lemon souffle dessert to die for with blueberry sauces, slickly presented.

Crisp cocktails: Negroni and Limoncello.

Modern look and feel, but not cold. Well lit, pretty tableware. A packed bar scene of very well-dressed people from their 20's to 70's.
reviews.author: Mike R.

reviews.text: Amanda, Ray and CJ  together made an amazing evening fantastic service, amazing food and a great host that made the evening possible. A must if you are in Scottsdale. Coming back tomorrow night.  Vegetable Bolognese off the hook.
reviews.author: Allen D.

reviews.text: Marcus and Natalia are absolutely fantastic! We love Giada and we're so excited to come check out Luna. The service they provided made the experience that much better! We will be back.
reviews.author: Sarah Z.

reviews.text: Bad martini glass, it towers over the whole table and the staff literally could not handle it. So tall, so top heavy, hard to drink out of. $22 before taxes and a 3.5% "admin venue fee." The drinks were rough, but it was opening night and I'm sure the bar tenders will get it together after some solid training.
reviews.author: Chris T.

reviews.text:
Bar: we started with a round of the signature cocktails. All of them were very sweet and it took a while to get our tab. 

Food: we ordered two appetizers. The fritto misto and bacon wrapped dates. Fritto misto was fine a little dry and overcooked. I wish they would have had a lemon to squeeze over it too since they emphasized lemon so much as a highlighted ingredient throughout the menu. The bacon wrapped dates were fine. 

The star of the entire experience was the focaccia. It was delicious and a little lighter than the typical focaccia which I loved! The mascarpone butter was also amazing 

The lemon pasta was fine a little heavy and starchy (photo shows a split portion) 

The scallop risotto was good, very rich and a little bland 

The agnolotti was probably the best of our entrees, but still left a lot to be desired. It was cold and bland, which unfortunately caused the flavor of the meats inside the pasta to be lost. 

We started with two classic cocktails a manhattan and an old fashion and both had to be sent back and remade. Our wine was great though 

Dessert was good, nothing special, we got the soufflé and one of the chocolate ones. 

Atmosphere: was nice clean and pretty but nothing extraordinary. They still have some finishing touches they need to work on. Bathroom missing a paper towel holder and the vent cover.

The staff was very accommodating as we asked to move tables. We were first sat in the back room by their private conference room. The back room felt a bit isolating since they still had furniture that hasn't arrived and overall lacked decor and ambiance. 

I hope this place can take these initial reviews and improve we went on opening night and I hope it was just opening night jitters. 

All of the staff were very kind :)
reviews.author: Amanda T.

reviews.text: Went to this restaurant opening night and I don't know if the quality was sub par because it was their first night or what... I got a few starters that were decent but I ordered the arrabbiata pasta which was way overcooked-the noodles were limp which was disappointing considering Giada herself was there herself but the upside was the waiter and staff were great and very attentive. The price was the most shocking, I will pay whatever for good food but not sub par Italian that's not cooked right.
reviews.author: Taylor M.

reviews.text:
This is our new go-to place! The whole experience was amazing from start to finish and I can't wait to be back! The whole staff was so on top of it to make sure we had the best experience- specifically the managers Ray and Keri and our server Tucker (he made great suggestions!). The restaurant is absolutely stunning with cute little touches from Giadas life and the kitchen was SPOTLESS. It a full open kitchen so it was awesome to see the team work together so well even in the first few days of being open. 
Now the important part- the food! 
We got a little bit of everything and every bite was so yummy! 
Highly suggest the crab arancini, margarita pizza, ANY of the pastas and the tiramisu or the cookies for dessert (the chocolate chip cookie was to die for!). 
Overall this was one of the best dinners we've had in Scottsdale. Highly suggest trying to get a reservation! You may even run into Giada.
reviews.author: Avery R.

reviews.text:
So, here's my take on Luna - It is a very attractive space, in a very attractive hotel. It has a great name behind it, in Giada. 

However,,, the food was very much blah. 

We tried the ravioli, arrabbiata  and a few starters. 

The ravioli was good, not great. 

The arrabbiata was entry level, at best. 

Limp pasta, weak flavors = big disappointment. 

Oh, let's not forget the price! Way aggressive for what is coming out of the kitchen.

reviews.author: Alex P.

reviews.text:
I was excited to try this restaurant, especially with so much hype behind it. First impressions, the hotel is beautiful and so is the restaurant. And it smells wonderful as most Vegas hotels do. The hostesses are very sweet and welcoming. The serving staff were all nice and attentive, although very slow to greet and bring out water and food. 

The food itself was subpar. To start the caprese salad came out as mushed watery mozzarella with a small amount of cherry tomatoes and some interesting "balsamic beads" on top. Although this was the best tasting thing I had, the portion was not worth the price ($23) Next was the spicy sausage pizza. Although the dough was thin and cooked well, it was such a small pizza with hardly any sauce and toppings. ($28) We also ordered the signature dish - a lemon spaghetti with shrimp. It was bland, underwhelming, not enough sauce, with 2 overcooked large shrimp on each side. The best part of the dish were the fried capers on top. Although the pasta was made in house, and cooked well the dish lacked flavor. Not worth the price and to be considered their specialty. ($39)

Other things to note: no bread service, a 3.5% venue admin charge on every check (apparently just because it's located inside the Caesar's hotel), a basic iced tea/soft drink will cost you $7, and the lighting still needs to be figured out. 

If you want to check out this new hotel, instead absolutely go upstairs to SEVEN. Their rooftop restaurant/bar on the 7th floor has incredible views of camelback and wayyy better food. (Try the wagyu sliders and salmon with cauliflower mash)
reviews.author: Melissa C.

reviews.text: What a beautiful restaurant! Dined her tonight and enjoyed the focaccia (which was to die for - we were told they made it in the pizza oven) the branzino (three generous pieces), the lemon spaghetti (my absolute favorite thing we tried - it came with two nice sized shrimp and we dipped the focaccia into the mascarpone Cheese sauce) omg it was INCREDIBLE!!! Our server, Tucker was top notch! Very attentive and charming! We saw a lot of other servers standing around looking like they didn't know where they should be or what they should be doing so it was kind of odd and I wish there were more wine options (I've never complained about a wine list before but there was ONE Chardonnay and it was $25 a glass) over all it was a great experience and I'm excited to see it grow!
